projects.name: Scalable, interpretable, and privacy-preserving feature engineering for federated learning: a systematic literature review
projects.description: This systematic review synthesizes 74 studies from 2020–2025 on feature engineering and feature selection across centralized, horizontal federated, vertical federated, and hybrid learning. It examines interpretability, privacy, fairness, compute and communication costs, and reproducibility, and identifies gaps in pipeline-level privacy accounting, end-to-end evaluation, and standardized benchmarks. This project includes an executable research demonstrator inspired by those themes: a reproducible horizontal-federated synthetic classification experiment with a bounded, named feature library, interpretable feature ranking, a record-level Laplace-private feature-selection query, in-process federated gradient aggregation, and accuracy and group-recall reporting. The demo is not a secure distributed deployment; only the feature-selection query is differentially private.
projects.publication_citation: Vijay Kumar Kambhampati and K. B. V. Brahma Rao. Scalable, interpretable, and privacy-preserving feature engineering for federated learning: a systematic literature review. Evolving Systems 17, 92 (2026). https://doi.org/10.1007/s12530-026-09852-8
